description: Standard neonatal clinical scoring systems used in NICU and postnatal care

interpretation.meaning: Normal
Moderate depression
Severe depression

scores.name: Combined Apgar Score

interpretation.meaning: The baby is adapting well. Higher scores mean fewer medical interventions were needed.
The baby is struggling. This score is a strong predictor of the need for NICU admission.
High risk for serious complications, including mortality or long-term neurological issues.

scores.reference: AAP Committee Opinion on Expanded Apgar Scoring; COMBED acronym — Carbajal & Texier 1997

interpretation.meaning: Mild distress
Moderate distress
Severe distress
No distress
Mild distress
Moderate distress
Severe distress

scores.name: Levene Staging (HIE)

interpretation.meaning: Good prognosis. Most infants recover fully with no or minimal neurological sequelae.
Variable outcome. Significant risk of neurodevelopmental impairment. Therapeutic hypothermia indicated if criteria met.
Poor prognosis. High risk of death or major neurodevelopmental disability.

scores.reference: Levene MI et al., Arch Dis Child 1985; HIE clinical staging based on neurological assessment

scores.name: IVH Grading (Papile & Volpe)

parameters.volpe: Germinal matrix hemorrhage with no IVH or IVH occupying <10% of the ventricular area on parasagittal view
IVH occupying 10–50% of the ventricular area on parasagittal view
IVH occupying >50% of the ventricular area on parasagittal view ± periventricular echodensities

parameters.papile: IVH extending into adjacent brain parenchyma
parameters.volpe: Periventricular venous hemorrhagic infarction (PVHI); cystic periventricular leukomalacia

interpretation.meaning: Mild. Generally good prognosis; low risk of post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus or neurodevelopmental sequelae.
Moderate. Significant risk of post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus; close neurodevelopmental follow-up required.
Severe. High risk of neurological disability and mortality; associated with periventricular venous infarction and leukomalacia.

scores.reference: Papile LA et al., J Pediatr 1978; Volpe JJ, Neurology of the Newborn 5th ed.

phvd.title: Post-Hemorrhagic Ventricular Dilatation (PHVD) — Management Zones

zones.name: Green Zone
zones.clinical_note: Absence of the following clinical criteria:
management: cUS twice a week until stable for 2 weeks then every 1-2 weeks till 34 weeks PMA

zones.name: Yellow Zone
zones.clinical_note: Absence of the following clinical criteria:
management: Referral to a regional center for neurosurgical review
cUS 2-3X a week until stable for 2 weeks then every 1-2 weeks till 34 weeks PMA
Neurosurgical intervention when no stabilization occurs

zones.name: Red Zone
zones.clinical_note: Any of the following clinical criteria:
management: Neurosurgical intervention including either temporizing measures or VP shunt

phvd.footer: Consider alterations in NIRS (ie decrease cerebral oxygenation) or Doppler US (ie Increase in Resistive Index) as additional information that may suggest impairment in cerebral perfusion and more urgent need for intervention.
phvd.reference: El-Dib, M., Limbrick, D. D., Jr, Inder, T., Whitelaw, A., Kulkarni, A. V., Warf, B., Volpe, J. J., & de Vries, L. S. (2020). Management of Post-hemorrhagic Ventricular Dilatation in the Infant Born Preterm. The Journal of Pediatrics, 226, 16–27.e3.

scores.name: Modified Sarnat Staging (HIE)

parameters.severe: Variable: often unequal, poor light reflex, fixed, dilated

interpretation.meaning: Full recovery expected. Hypoxic-ischaemic episode usually transient. No or minimal long-term sequelae.
Variable outcome. Significant risk of neurodevelopmental disability. Therapeutic hypothermia (cooling) indicated if criteria met.
Poor prognosis. High mortality. Survivors at high risk of major neurodevelopmental disability including cerebral palsy.

scores.reference: Sarnat HB & Sarnat MS, Arch Neurol 1976; Modified by Levene et al. * Tonic neck reflex: elicited by rotating head to one side — ipsilateral arm/leg extend, contralateral flex ("fencing" posture).

scores.name: Thompson Score (HIE)

interpretation.meaning: Mild HIE
Moderate HIE
Severe HIE

scores.reference: Thompson CM et al., Acta Paediatrica 1997. Maximum score: 22 (scoring 0–3 per sign; Fits, Moro, Grasp, Suck, Fontanelle max 2)

scores.name: LATCH Score (Breastfeeding)

interpretation.meaning: Higher score = better breastfeeding effectiveness

scores.reference: Jensen D et al., J Obstet Gynecol Neonatal Nurs 1994

scores.name: BIND Score (Bilirubin-Induced Neurologic Dysfunction)

parameters.2: Lethargic, poor suck and/or irritable/jittery with strong suck
parameters.3: Semi-coma, apnoea, unable to feed, seizures, coma

parameters.2: Mild to moderate hypertonia alternating with hypotonia, beginning arching of neck and trunk on stimulation
parameters.3: Persistent retrocollis and opisthotonus, bicycling or twitching of hands and feet

interpretation.meaning: No signs of bilirubin-induced neurologic dysfunction.
Subtle, usually reversible ABE. Intensify phototherapy and reassess frequently.
Moderate, usually reversible ABE. Treat urgently — intensive phototherapy and prepare for exchange transfusion.
Advanced ABE, usually irreversible. Emergency exchange transfusion.

scores.reference: Johnson L, Bhutani VK, Brown AK. Journal of Pediatrics 2002; BIND score for acute bilirubin encephalopathy. Assessed serially; the total, not one item, drives urgency.

scores.name: CRIES Pain Score (Neonatal)

parameters.0: No cry, or cry that is not high-pitched
Heart rate and blood pressure at or below baseline
parameters.1: Heart rate or blood pressure up to 20% above baseline
parameters.2: Heart rate or blood pressure more than 20% above baseline

interpretation.meaning: No or minimal pain. Continue routine comfort measures.
Mild to moderate pain. Non-pharmacological measures first — swaddling, sucrose, containment, skin-to-skin.
Moderate to severe pain. Treat, and reassess after the intervention. A score of 4 or more is the usual trigger for analgesia.

scores.reference: Krechel SW, Bildner J. CRIES: a new neonatal postoperative pain measurement score. Paediatr Anaesth. 1995;5(1):53-61. Validated for neonates from 32 weeks gestation; measure vital signs LAST, as handling raises them.

scores.name: NIPS — Neonatal Infant Pain Scale

parameters.0: Relaxed muscles — restful face, neutral expression
parameters.1: Grimace — tight facial muscles, furrowed brow, chin and jaw

parameters.2: Vigorous cry — loud scream, rising, shrill, continuous

parameters.0: Relaxed — usual pattern for this infant
parameters.1: Change in breathing — indrawing, irregular, faster, gagging, breath-holding

parameters.0: Relaxed or restrained — no muscular rigidity, occasional random movement
parameters.1: Flexed or extended — tense, straight arms, rigid or rapid extension and flexion

parameters.0: Relaxed or restrained — no muscular rigidity, occasional random movement
parameters.1: Flexed or extended — tense, straight legs, rigid or rapid extension and flexion

parameters.0: Sleeping or awake — quiet, peaceful, sleeping, or alert and settled

interpretation.meaning: No or minimal pain. Continue routine comfort measures.
Borderline. Reassess after a non-pharmacological measure — swaddling, containment, sucrose, skin-to-skin.
Pain present. A score above 3 indicates pain. Treat, then reassess after the intervention.

scores.reference: Lawrence J, Alcock D, McGrath P, Kay J, MacMurray SB, Dulberg C. The development of a tool to assess neonatal pain. Neonatal Netw. 1993;12(6):59-66. Six behavioural and physiological items; maximum 7. A score above 3 indicates pain. Note the items are NOT all scored alike — cry scores 0-2, every other item 0-1.

scores.name: PIPP — Premature Infant Pain Profile

parameters.parameter: Behavioural state (observe 15 s before the procedure)
parameters.0: Active and awake — eyes open, facial movements
parameters.1: Quiet and awake — eyes open, no facial movements
parameters.2: Active and asleep — eyes closed, facial movements
parameters.3: Quiet and asleep — eyes closed, no facial movements
Maximum — 70% or more of the time
Maximum — 70% or more of the time
Maximum — 70% or more of the time

interpretation.meaning: Minimal or no pain. Routine comfort measures.
Mild to moderate pain. Non-pharmacological measures first; reassess.
Moderate to severe pain. Treat and reassess after the intervention.

scores.reference: Stevens B, Johnston C, Petryshen P, Taddio A. Premature Infant Pain Profile: development and initial validation. Clin J Pain. 1996;12(1):13-22. Seven indicators, each 0-3; maximum 21. Gestational age and behavioural state are CONTEXTUAL — score them before the procedure. Heart rate and saturation are scored as the CHANGE from the infant’s own baseline over 30 seconds, not as absolute values. A revised version (PIPP-R) exists.

scores.name: Neonatal Skin Condition Score (NSCS)

parameters.1: Normal — no sign of dry skin
parameters.3: Very dry skin — cracking or fissures

parameters.2: Visible erythema over less than 50% of the body surface
parameters.3: Visible erythema over 50% or more of the body surface

interpretation.meaning: Best possible skin condition. Continue routine skin care.
Mild disruption. Review emollient use, humidity, adhesive removal technique and positioning.
Moderate disruption. Active skin-care plan; reassess at least daily.
Most disrupted skin condition. Minimise adhesives and handling, protect pressure areas, involve senior nursing review.

scores.reference: Lund CH, Osborne JW. Validity and reliability of the Neonatal Skin Condition Score. J Obstet Gynecol Neonatal Nurs. 2004;33(3):320-7. Developed for the AWHONN/NANN neonatal skin care evidence-based practice project. Three items scored 1-3 each, so the score runs 3 (best) to 9 (worst) — the minimum is 3, not 0.

scores.name: nSOFA — Neonatal Sequential Organ Failure Assessment

parameters.0: Not intubated, or intubated with SpO₂/FiO₂ ratio 300 or more
No inotropes and no systemic corticosteroid
parameters.3: Two or more inotropes, OR one inotrope with a systemic corticosteroid
parameters.4: Two or more inotropes with a systemic corticosteroid

interpretation.meaning: No organ dysfunction scored on any of the three domains.
Low organ-dysfunction burden.
Moderate organ-dysfunction burden. Rising scores carry rising mortality risk.
High organ-dysfunction burden. Escalate assessment and support.

scores.reference: Wynn JL, Polin RA. A neonatal sequential organ failure assessment score predicts mortality to late-onset sepsis in preterm very low birth weight infants. Pediatr Res. 2020;88(1):85-90. Three domains; maximum 15. IMPORTANT: nSOFA is validated as a CONTINUOUS predictor of mortality — the bands above describe the magnitude of the score, they are not validated treatment thresholds, and published cut-offs vary with population and timing. The respiratory domain scores only 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8; the cardiovascular domain 0-4; platelets 0-3.

scores.name: Modified Sick Neonatal Score (MSNS)

parameters.1: Tachypnoea (respiratory rate above 60/min) with or without retractions

interpretation.meaning: HIGH mortality risk. A score of 10 or below predicted mortality with 80% sensitivity and 88.8% specificity. Escalate care.
Intermediate. Close monitoring and reassessment.
Lower mortality risk. Discharged infants averaged around 14 in the derivation study.

scores.reference: Mansoor KP, Ravikiran SR, Kulkarni V, et al. Modified Sick Neonatal Score (MSNS): a novel neonatal disease severity scoring system for resource-limited settings. Crit Care Res Pract. 2019;2019:9059073. WARNING — THIS SCORE RUNS BACKWARDS: a HIGHER score is BETTER. Eight parameters scored 0–2 each, maximum 16, and it is a LOW score that predicts mortality (cut-off 10 or below). Do not read it like the pain or severity scores in this list, where a high number is the bad one.
